aspirin: Salicylate NSAID; at low dose an irreversible antiplatelet used for cardiovascular protection.
ibuprofen: Widely used over-the-counter NSAID for pain, fever and inflammation.
naproxen: Longer-acting NSAID favoured for musculoskeletal pain.
diclofenac: Potent NSAID available orally and topically.
celecoxib: COX-2-selective NSAID with less GI toxicity.
ketorolac: Strong short-term NSAID for acute pain.
indomethacin: Potent NSAID also used for acute gout and closure of patent ductus arteriosus.
etoricoxib: COX-2-selective NSAID used for arthritis and acute gout.
paracetamol: Acetaminophen; first-line analgesic/antipyretic with negligible anti-inflammatory action.
codeine: Weak opioid pro-drug; also an antitussive.
tramadol: Weak opioid with monoamine-reuptake action for moderate pain.
oxycodone: Strong oral opioid for moderate-to-severe pain.
fentanyl: Very potent synthetic opioid; anaesthetic adjunct and transdermal analgesic.
buprenorphine: Partial opioid agonist for pain and opioid dependence.
methadone: Long-acting opioid for chronic pain and opioid-dependence maintenance.
ergotamine: Ergot alkaloid for migraine (largely superseded by triptans).
allopurinol: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowering urate for chronic gout.
febuxostat: Non-purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor for gout.
colchicine: Anti-inflammatory alkaloid for acute gout and familial Mediterranean fever.
probenecid: Uricosuric that increases renal urate excretion.
methotrexate: Antifolate: low-dose DMARD for rheumatoid arthritis/psoriasis, high-dose chemotherapy.
hydroxychloroquine: Antimalarial also used as a DMARD in lupus and rheumatoid arthritis.
sulfasalazine: Used both as a DMARD and for inflammatory bowel disease.
leflunomide: Pyrimidine-synthesis inhibitor DMARD for rheumatoid arthritis.
azathioprine: Purine-synthesis inhibitor for transplantation and autoimmune disease.
tacrolimus: Potent calcineurin inhibitor for transplantation and eczema.
mycophenolate mofetil: Inhibits lymphocyte purine synthesis; transplant immunosuppression.
adalimumab: Anti-TNF monoclonal antibody for rheumatoid arthritis, IBD, psoriasis.
etanercept: TNF-receptor fusion protein for inflammatory arthritis.
infliximab: Anti-TNF monoclonal antibody for IBD and inflammatory arthritis.
prednisolone: Widely used oral glucocorticoid for inflammation and immunosuppression.
dexamethasone: Potent long-acting glucocorticoid; also antiemetic and used in severe COVID-19.
hydrocortisone: Short-acting glucocorticoid; physiological replacement and topical use.
methylprednisolone: Intermediate-acting glucocorticoid, often given IV in flares.
betamethasone: Potent glucocorticoid used topically and for fetal lung maturation.
triamcinolone: Glucocorticoid for intra-articular, topical and inhaled use.
lisinopril: Long-acting ACE inhibitor for hypertension and heart failure.
ramipril: ACE inhibitor with strong cardiovascular-protection evidence.
enalapril: ACE-inhibitor pro-drug for hypertension and heart failure.
perindopril: Long-acting ACE inhibitor for hypertension and coronary disease.
losartan: First angiotensin-receptor blocker; also mildly uricosuric.
valsartan: ARB for hypertension and heart failure.
candesartan: Long-acting ARB; also used in migraine prophylaxis.
irbesartan: ARB with evidence in diabetic nephropathy.
metoprolol: Cardioselective β-blocker for angina, arrhythmia and heart failure.
atenolol: Cardioselective β-blocker for hypertension and angina.
bisoprolol: Highly cardioselective β-blocker with heart-failure evidence.
carvedilol: Combined α/β-blocker used in chronic heart failure.
propranolol: Non-selective β-blocker; also for tremor, anxiety and migraine prophylaxis.
labetalol: Combined α/β-blocker used in hypertension of pregnancy.
amlodipine: Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker for hypertension/angina.
nifedipine: Dihydropyridine CCB; also used for Raynaud's and preterm labour.
diltiazem: Non-dihydropyridine CCB that also slows the heart rate.
verapamil: Rate-limiting CCB for arrhythmia and angina.
furosemide: Loop diuretic for oedema and heart failure.
bumetanide: Potent loop diuretic, alternative to furosemide.
chlortalidone: Long-acting thiazide-like diuretic with strong outcome data.
spironolactone: Aldosterone antagonist ('potassium-sparing'); heart failure and resistant hypertension.
eplerenone: Selective aldosterone antagonist used post-MI and in heart failure.
amiloride: Potassium-sparing diuretic, usually combined with a thiazide.
amiodarone: Broad-spectrum antiarrhythmic for atrial and ventricular arrhythmias.
digoxin: Cardiac glycoside for rate control in AF and for heart failure.
flecainide: Class Ic antiarrhythmic for AF in structurally normal hearts.
sotalol: β-blocker with additional class III antiarrhythmic action.
adenosine: Ultra-short-acting agent to terminate supraventricular tachycardia.
glyceryl trinitrate: Rapid nitrate vasodilator for acute angina.
isosorbide mononitrate: Long-acting oral nitrate for angina prophylaxis.
atorvastatin: Potent, widely used statin lowering LDL cholesterol.
pravastatin: Hydrophilic statin with fewer drug interactions.
ezetimibe: Blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption; added to statins.
evolocumab: PCSK9-inhibitor monoclonal antibody for very high LDL.
ticagrelor: Reversible P2Y12 inhibitor for acute coronary syndrome.
prasugrel: Potent P2Y12 inhibitor used with PCI.
dipyridamole: Antiplatelet/vasodilator, often combined with aspirin for stroke prevention.
warfarin: Vitamin-K-antagonist oral anticoagulant requiring INR monitoring.
apixaban: Direct oral factor Xa inhibitor with favourable bleeding profile.
doxazosin: α1-blocker for hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia.
prazosin: α1-blocker; also used for PTSD-related nightmares.
clonidine: Central α2-agonist for hypertension, ADHD and withdrawal states.
methyldopa: Central antihypertensive of choice in pregnancy.
hydralazine: Arterial vasodilator for hypertension and heart failure.
minoxidil: Potent vasodilator; topically stimulates hair growth.
ivabradine: Slows heart rate via the sinus-node If current in heart failure/angina.
amoxicillin: Broad-spectrum aminopenicillin, a first-line oral antibiotic.
ampicillin: Aminopenicillin used IV for a range of infections.
benzylpenicillin: Injectable penicillin G for streptococcal and meningococcal infection.
phenoxymethylpenicillin: Oral penicillin V for streptococcal throat/skin infections.
ceftriaxone: Third-generation cephalosporin for serious infection and meningitis.
meropenem: Very broad-spectrum carbapenem for severe infection.
azithromycin: Long-half-life macrolide for respiratory, skin and STI infections.
clarithromycin: Macrolide used in respiratory infection and H. pylori eradication.
erythromycin: Classic macrolide; also a gut prokinetic at low dose.
doxycycline: Broad tetracycline for chest, skin, tick-borne infection and malaria prophylaxis.
minocycline: Tetracycline used for acne and resistant infections.
gentamicin: Aminoglycoside for serious Gram-negative sepsis (levels monitored).
amikacin: Aminoglycoside active against many resistant Gram-negatives.
tobramycin: Aminoglycoside, including inhaled use in cystic fibrosis.
co-trimoxazole: Sulfamethoxazole plus trimethoprim; UTIs and Pneumocystis pneumonia.
trimethoprim: Folate-pathway antibiotic, first-line for uncomplicated UTIs.
vancomycin: Glycopeptide for MRSA and other resistant Gram-positive infection.
metronidazole: Antibiotic/antiprotozoal for anaerobes, C. difficile and amoebiasis.
clindamycin: Lincosamide for anaerobic and Gram-positive infection.
linezolid: Oxazolidinone active against MRSA and VRE.
rifampicin: Key antitubercular; also for staphylococcal and meningococcal prophylaxis.
chloramphenicol: Broad antibiotic reserved for serious infection; common as eye drops.
aciclovir: Antiviral for herpes simplex and varicella-zoster.
tenofovir: Nucleotide reverse-transcriptase inhibitor for HIV and hepatitis B.
emtricitabine: NRTI, a backbone of HIV therapy and PrEP.
dolutegravir: Integrase inhibitor, a preferred anchor of modern HIV therapy.
lamivudine: NRTI for HIV and hepatitis B.
ritonavir: Protease inhibitor used mainly as a pharmacokinetic booster.
fluconazole: Triazole antifungal for candidiasis and cryptococcosis.
itraconazole: Broad triazole antifungal including for aspergillosis.
voriconazole: Triazole of choice for invasive aspergillosis.
amphotericin b: Polyene for severe systemic fungal infection.
terbinafine: Allylamine antifungal for dermatophyte nail/skin infection.
clotrimazole: Topical imidazole for thrush and ringworm.
artemether: Artemisinin derivative, given with lumefantrine for falciparum malaria.
artesunate: First-line parenteral treatment for severe malaria.
primaquine: Clears liver hypnozoites of vivax/ovale malaria.
quinine: Old antimalarial still used for resistant/severe cases.
pyrazinamide: First-line antitubercular used in the initial phase.
ivermectin: Antiparasitic for onchocerciasis, strongyloidiasis and scabies.
praziquantel: Drug of choice for schistosomiasis and tapeworms.
tinidazole: Nitroimidazole for giardiasis, amoebiasis and trichomoniasis.
paroxetine: Potent SSRI with notable discontinuation effects.
duloxetine: SNRI for depression, anxiety and neuropathic pain.
amitriptyline: Tricyclic used at low dose for neuropathic pain and migraine, higher for depression.
clomipramine: Tricyclic with strong serotonergic action, used in OCD.
phenelzine: Irreversible MAO inhibitor for refractory depression.
moclobemide: Reversible MAO-A inhibitor with fewer dietary restrictions.
bupropion: Dopamine/noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor for depression and smoking cessation.
trazodone: Sedating antidepressant often used for insomnia.
haloperidol: High-potency typical antipsychotic; also for delirium and nausea.
risperidone: Atypical antipsychotic for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
olanzapine: Atypical antipsychotic; also used for chemotherapy-induced nausea.
quetiapine: Sedating atypical antipsychotic used across mood and psychotic disorders.
clozapine: Most effective antipsychotic for resistant schizophrenia (needs blood monitoring).
diazepam: Long-acting benzodiazepine for anxiety, spasm, seizures and alcohol withdrawal.
lorazepam: Intermediate-acting benzodiazepine; first-line for status epilepticus.
clonazepam: Long-acting benzodiazepine for seizures and anxiety.
midazolam: Short-acting benzodiazepine for sedation and procedures.
buspirone: Non-sedating 5-HT1A partial agonist for generalised anxiety.
lithium: Classic mood stabiliser for bipolar disorder (narrow therapeutic index).
carbamazepine: Antiepileptic, mood stabiliser and treatment for trigeminal neuralgia.
gabapentin: Antiepileptic widely used for neuropathic pain.
pregabalin: Used for neuropathic pain, epilepsy and generalised anxiety.
topiramate: Antiepileptic also used for migraine prophylaxis.
levodopa: Dopamine precursor (with carbidopa) — the cornerstone of Parkinson's therapy.
ropinirole: Dopamine agonist for Parkinson's disease and restless legs.
pramipexole: Dopamine agonist for Parkinson's disease and restless legs.
selegiline: MAO-B inhibitor used in Parkinson's disease.
amantadine: Antiparkinson agent (dyskinesia) with historical antiviral use.
rivastigmine: Cholinesterase inhibitor (oral/patch) for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's dementia.
memantine: NMDA-receptor antagonist for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease.
caffeine: The world's most-used stimulant; also treats apnoea of prematurity.
melatonin: Hormone supplement for insomnia and jet lag.
propofol: Intravenous agent for induction/maintenance of anaesthesia and ICU sedation.
ketamine: Dissociative anaesthetic; also rapid-acting for resistant depression.
sevoflurane: Inhaled volatile anaesthetic, common for induction in children.
lidocaine: Most-used local anaesthetic; also a class Ib antiarrhythmic.
bupivacaine: Long-acting local anaesthetic for regional/epidural blocks.
ropivacaine: Long-acting local anaesthetic with less cardiotoxicity.
tizanidine: Central α2-agonist muscle relaxant for spasticity.
suxamethonium: Depolarising neuromuscular blocker for rapid intubation.
metformin: First-line oral drug for type 2 diabetes; reduces hepatic glucose output.
linagliptin: DPP-4 inhibitor not requiring renal dose adjustment.
empagliflozin: SGLT2 inhibitor lowering glucose and improving heart-failure/renal outcomes.
dapagliflozin: SGLT2 inhibitor with heart-failure and chronic-kidney-disease indications.
liraglutide: Daily GLP-1 agonist for diabetes and obesity.
semaglutide: Weekly GLP-1 agonist (oral/injectable) for diabetes and weight loss.
dulaglutide: Weekly GLP-1 agonist for type 2 diabetes.
levothyroxine: Synthetic T4; standard replacement for hypothyroidism.
carbimazole: Antithyroid drug for hyperthyroidism (pro-drug of methimazole).
propylthiouracil: Antithyroid drug, preferred in the first trimester of pregnancy.
ethinylestradiol: Synthetic oestrogen, the oestrogen component of most combined contraceptives.
levonorgestrel: Progestogen used in contraceptives and emergency contraception.
estradiol: Bioidentical oestrogen for hormone replacement therapy.
finasteride: 5α-reductase inhibitor for benign prostatic hyperplasia and hair loss.
tamoxifen: Selective oestrogen-receptor modulator for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer.
zoledronic acid: Potent IV bisphosphonate for osteoporosis and bone metastases.
denosumab: Anti-RANKL antibody for osteoporosis and bone metastases.
salmeterol: Long-acting β2-agonist (with an inhaled steroid) for maintenance.
terbutaline: β2-agonist bronchodilator; also used as a uterine relaxant.
fluticasone: Inhaled/intranasal corticosteroid for asthma and rhinitis.
budesonide: Inhaled steroid for asthma; oral formulations for Crohn's disease.
montelukast: Oral leukotriene-receptor antagonist for asthma and allergic rhinitis.
fexofenadine: Non-sedating antihistamine, active metabolite of terfenadine.
diphenhydramine: Sedating first-generation antihistamine; also an OTC sleep aid and antiemetic.
chlorphenamine: Sedating antihistamine for allergy and anaphylaxis adjunct.
promethazine: Sedating antihistamine used for nausea, allergy and as a sedative.
hydroxyzine: Sedating antihistamine used for itch and anxiety.
oxymetazoline: Topical nasal decongestant (limit to a few days).
acetylcysteine: Mucolytic; also the antidote for paracetamol overdose.
omeprazole: Prototype proton pump inhibitor for reflux and ulcers.
ranitidine: H2-receptor antagonist for acid reduction (withdrawn in many markets).
ondansetron: 5-HT3 antagonist for chemotherapy- and surgery-related nausea.
domperidone: Peripheral dopamine antagonist; antiemetic and prokinetic.
cyclizine: Antihistamine antiemetic for motion sickness and vomiting.
prochlorperazine: Phenothiazine used mainly as an antiemetic and for vertigo.
loperamide: Opioid-receptor agonist acting locally in the gut to slow motility.
lactulose: Osmotic laxative; also lowers ammonia in hepatic encephalopathy.
hyoscine butylbromide: Antimuscarinic for GI/urinary cramp; hyoscine also treats motion sickness.
mebeverine: Direct smooth-muscle relaxant for irritable bowel syndrome.
sildenafil: PDE5 inhibitor for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension.
tadalafil: Long-acting PDE5 inhibitor; also for BPH symptoms.
tamsulosin: Uroselective α1-blocker for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
cisplatin: Platinum alkylating-like agent central to many chemotherapy regimens.
carboplatin: Platinum agent, less nephrotoxic than cisplatin.
cyclophosphamide: Alkylating agent used in cancer and severe autoimmune disease.
paclitaxel: Taxane that stabilises microtubules; broad solid-tumour use.
fluorouracil: Antimetabolite (5-FU) for GI and other cancers.
gemcitabine: Antimetabolite for pancreatic and other cancers.
vincristine: Vinca alkaloid used in leukaemia and lymphoma.
imatinib: BCR-ABL tyrosine-kinase inhibitor that transformed chronic myeloid leukaemia.
erlotinib: EGFR tyrosine-kinase inhibitor for lung cancer.
osimertinib: Third-generation EGFR inhibitor for EGFR-mutant lung cancer.
trastuzumab: Anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody for HER2-positive breast cancer.
rituximab: Anti-CD20 antibody for lymphomas and autoimmune disease.
anastrozole: Aromatase inhibitor for postmenopausal breast cancer.
letrozole: Aromatase inhibitor for breast cancer; also used for ovulation induction.
leuprorelin: GnRH agonist for prostate cancer and endometriosis.
pembrolizumab: Anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor across many cancers.
ascorbic acid: Vitamin C; antioxidant and cofactor, treats scurvy.
cholecalciferol: Vitamin D3 for deficiency and bone health.
folic acid: Vitamin B9; prevents neural-tube defects and treats deficiency anaemia.
pyridoxine: Vitamin B6; co-given with isoniazid and for deficiency.
phytomenadione: Vitamin K1; reverses warfarin and prevents newborn bleeding.
calcium carbonate: Calcium supplement that also neutralises stomach acid.
naloxone: Opioid-receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid overdose.
naltrexone: Long-acting opioid antagonist for opioid/alcohol dependence.
atropine: Antimuscarinic for bradycardia, organophosphate poisoning and secretions.
adrenaline: Epinephrine; first-line for anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest.
glucagon: Raises blood glucose in severe hypoglycaemia; also for beta-blocker overdose.
acetaminophen: Acetaminophen; first-line analgesic/antipyretic with negligible anti-inflammatory action.
nitroglycerin: Rapid nitrate vasodilator for acute angina.
sulfamethoxazole: Sulfamethoxazole plus trimethoprim; UTIs and Pneumocystis pneumonia.
rifampin: Key antitubercular; also for staphylococcal and meningococcal prophylaxis.
acyclovir: Antiviral for herpes simplex and varicella-zoster.
tenofovir disoproxil: Nucleotide reverse-transcriptase inhibitor for HIV and hepatitis B.
succinylcholine: Depolarising neuromuscular blocker for rapid intubation.
chlorpheniramine: Sedating antihistamine for allergy and anaphylaxis adjunct.
scopolamine butylbromide: Antimuscarinic for GI/urinary cramp; hyoscine also treats motion sickness.
leuprolide: GnRH agonist for prostate cancer and endometriosis.
phytonadione: Vitamin K1; reverses warfarin and prevents newborn bleeding.
epinephrine: Epinephrine; first-line for anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest.
